title: Major vs Minor Ear Training
description: Schema-ready ear training for hearing major and minor triads.
overview: Major chords usually sound bright or settled. Minor chords usually sound darker or more serious.
goal: Choose whether the played chord is major or minor.
instructions: First, listen to labeled examples of major and minor chords.
Use Continue after each example when the sound is clear.
In the quiz steps, listen to the chord and choose major or minor.

challenges.label: Learn the major sound
challenges.hint: Major chords often sound bright, open, or settled.

challenges.label: Learn the minor sound
challenges.hint: Minor chords often sound darker, sadder, or more serious.

challenges.label: Listen and choose the chord quality
challenges.hint: Do not worry about the chord name yet. Decide whether the overall quality is major or minor.

challenges.label: Listen and choose the chord quality
challenges.hint: Compare this sound to the major example you heard earlier.

challenges.label: Listen and choose the chord quality
challenges.hint: This uses a different root, so focus on quality instead of pitch height.
